title: The Field Day
teaser: Five tryouts, one gold medal, and the dog does the judging.
clue: Nobody is racing anybody. The gold goes to whatever your dog loves best.
reveal: Run five one-minute auditions in your fenced yard and watch which one your dog leans into. The winner gets a drawn medal and a victory encore. Every dog medals in something.
objective: Offer five gentle one-minute events in your yard, tally your dog's own enthusiasm, and award the medal to their favorite.
instructions: Use your fenced yard. Check it is not hot (see the safety lines), the grass is dry and grippy, and the ground is clear of glass and sharp things.

Write five event cards: Sniff Scatter, Soft Roll, Towel Find, Flag Stroll and Free Browse. Put a bowl of water and a shade spot (a blanket or shady corner) as the rest stop, and draw a tally sheet with three columns: 'leaned in', 'joined briefly', 'passed'.

Sniff Scatter: scatter five or six pieces of the day's ration across a few square feet of your own lawn (or press them into a snuffle mat). Soft Roll: roll a soft ball bigger than your dog's mouth along the ground about five steps. Towel Find: put a toy under a towel in plain view. Flag Stroll: walk a slow line past four towels laid on the grass. Free Browse: let your dog roam the yard.
Run one event at a time for a minute or two, then rest and offer water. Tick the column that matches your dog's reaction. If they are not into one, say nothing and move on: passing is also an answer.
Add up the ticks. The event with the most 'leaned in' takes gold, the next silver. Draw a medal and announce the verdict.
Hold a one-minute victory encore of the gold event, then finish with water and rest in the shade.
twist: Every event is an audition, not a contest: your dog's own enthusiasm picks the gold, so a sniffer, a roller and a loafer all take home a medal.
variations: For a dog who already loves discs: swap Soft Roll for a soft, flexible disc rolled along the ground like a wheel, with no air throws and stop if they leap.
For a seated owner: do the five events in a small area and stay on a chair.
For a senior or slower dog: shorten each event to thirty seconds and add a longer rest after each.
For a food-free day: use toys for Sniff Scatter and Towel Find.
completion: Your dog has tried at least three events and a gold medal has been awarded.
photoIdea: Photograph your dog with the paper medal on the grass, relaxed, from a low angle.
memoryPrompt: Which event took gold, and which one did your dog ignore?
dietNotes: Sniff Scatter uses a few pieces counted from the day's ration. Ask your vet about your dog's diet. For a food-free version use a toy instead.
safety: Skip hot days and hot ground: check with the back of your hand for five seconds, and always have shade and water.
Keep every event gentle: no jumping, sharp turns or chasing at speed, and rest between them.
Use only a fully fenced yard, stay with your dog the whole time, and run one dog at a time.
